label_definitions.Verified: Taken directly from a published guideline or consensus report, cited with DOI.

ADA_KDIGO_2022.title: Diabetes Management in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Consensus Report by the ADA and KDIGO

ESC_HF_2023.title: 2023 Focused Update of the 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure
ESC_HF_2023.authors: McDonagh TA, Metra M, et al.
ESC_HF_2023.journal: Eur J Heart Fail 2024;26(1):5-17 (also Eur Heart J 2023)

AHA_HF_2022.title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
AHA_HF_2022.authors: Heidenreich PA, Bozkurt B, et al.

cards.guideline_says: People with type 2 diabetes should be screened for CKD at least once a year, starting at diagnosis. Screening includes both urine albumin (UACR) and eGFR.
cards.question_for_clinician: When were the eGFR and urine albumin (UACR) last checked, and what were the results?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: An SGLT2 inhibitor is recommended for people with type 2 diabetes and CKD when eGFR is at least 20. Once started, it can usually be continued at lower eGFR unless not tolerated or dialysis starts.
cards.question_for_clinician: Is an SGLT2 inhibitor appropriate given the latest eGFR, and if one is already prescribed, should it continue?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: The 2023 ESC focused update gives SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) a Class I, Level A recommendation to reduce heart failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, and in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD.
cards.question_for_clinician: Given the heart failure type and ejection fraction, would an SGLT2 inhibitor lower the risk of hospitalization?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: Metformin is recommended in type 2 diabetes with CKD when eGFR is at least 30. The dose should be reduced to 1000 mg per day when eGFR is 30 to 44.
cards.question_for_clinician: Does the current metformin dose still fit the latest eGFR?
cards.label: Verified

cards.topic: ACE inhibitor or ARB with albuminuria
cards.guideline_says: An ACE inhibitor or ARB is recommended for people with diabetes who have high blood pressure and albuminuria, titrated to the highest tolerated dose. Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB is not advised because of high potassium and acute kidney injury risk.
cards.question_for_clinician: Is there albuminuria, and is the blood pressure medicine an ACE inhibitor or ARB at the highest tolerated dose?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: Finerenone (a nonsteroidal MRA) is recommended for people with type 2 diabetes, eGFR of at least 25, normal potassium, and albuminuria (ACR of 30 mg/g or more) despite the maximum tolerated dose of an ACE inhibitor or ARB.
cards.question_for_clinician: If albuminuria persists on an ACE inhibitor or ARB, is finerenone an option, and what do the potassium levels show?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: A GLP-1 receptor agonist is recommended for people with type 2 diabetes and CKD who do not meet their individualized glucose target with metformin and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor, preferring an agent with proven cardiovascular benefit.
cards.question_for_clinician: Is the A1C at its individual target, and if not, would a GLP-1 receptor agonist with cardiovascular benefit fit?
cards.label: Verified

cards.guideline_says: ADA recommends a blood pressure target below 130/80 for people with diabetes and high blood pressure at high cardiovascular risk, if it can be reached safely.
cards.question_for_clinician: What is the blood pressure target for this person, and are home readings meeting it?
cards.label: Verified

cards.topic: SGLT2 inhibitor in reduced ejection fraction
cards.guideline_says: The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline gives SGLT2 inhibitors a Class 1 recommendation in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction to reduce hospitalization and cardiovascular death, whether or not the person has type 2 diabetes.
cards.question_for_clinician: If the ejection fraction is reduced, is an SGLT2 inhibitor part of the heart failure treatment plan?
cards.label: Verified
